title: Rent party prices, bootleg drink and learning to drink
summary: Albertson asks about the parties; Wooding gives prices, mentions blackberry and gin, and a friend's mother warning them apart.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Before we go on, what about these rent parties. Were they in Philadelphia or Atlantic City?
I was very seldom in Atlantic City in the wintertime, because we was only down there with my father. See, and he worked and when Labor Day, then we all came home.
Well, how much did they charge, then, at these parties?

Ten cents at the party, and then it worked up. High toned parties got a quarter. And then you had to buy your own pigs feet and potato salad. And the people started bringing a little bootleg, and a little blackberry and gin, and things like that, and whisky, in the bottle parlor, so that
a fellow -- you'd pay a quarter for a drink, and like that's where I learned how to drink. And then one day I got ahold of some blackberry and gin, and it tasted kind of good, and I had one too many.

Another time, another a friend of mine, he went overboard. But, one thing, I never did go overboard. But this fellow went overboard, and we took him home, we were all kids and we was afraid to let his people know it, so we stood him up on the steps and we told him to hold on to the doorknob and we rang the bell and run. So, when he come to the door, they find him out there, and that didn't work in my favor because, after all, she, his mother, told him, "See here, I want you to stay away from that old Sammy Wood -- Wooding", she said, "because he ain't no good. If you all hang together you know the first thing --"., And I come home and my mother told me the same thing, "Want you to stay away from Maceo White, because if you hang with him --", but we was learnin' how to play together, we was studyin' together, so and then she told me, "You'd better stay away from him because he ain't goin' to get you in any trouble."
So then we went on through high school.
